content:
Maya (Product): FinReg follow-up — they want per-tenant + per-route cost tile in the console, downloadable trace exports for audits, and a signed redaction attestation. Need to agree MVP scope and tradeoffs.
Liam (Eng): Token-level billing is expensive. Proposal: estimate cost per request (token_count estimate * cost_per_token) + deterministic sampled traces. No per-token lineage for MVP.
Ethan (SRE): Ops notes: major cost levers are retention and export egress. Suggest hot storage 14d for UI queries, cold exportable store 90d. Sampling rate defaults to 1% but tenant-configurable.
Nadia (Security): Redaction must be provable. We should log redaction events as counts + hashes, never raw PII. Exports should be signed (HMAC) and include a redaction report.
Priya (Compliance): For the pilot we can provide a compliance-signed report, production requires signed attestations. Need to capture which regexes/patterns were applied and when.
Ravi (Customer Success): FinReg will accept CSV but prefers parquet for schema consistency. They also want a date-range filter and tenant selector. Latency impact is a concern — they asked for assurance that tracing won't spike tail latency.
Sam (Solutions): UI mock: compact tile "Audit Cost & Traces" -> modal with: top cost chart (7d/30d), sampled traces list, export button (CSV/Parquet), redaction status badge. Keep filters minimal for MVP.
Maya (Product): MVP cuts I'm proposing: 1) Aggregated per-route cost (7d + 30d views), 2) Stable deterministic sampling of traces (configurable 0.5%–2%), 3) Redaction service that runs before storage + redaction verification report, 4) Tenant opt-in pilot (1 customer). Launch criteria: pilot ingest working, compliance sign-off, perf impact validated (<2% p99). Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Liam (Eng): Implementation sketch: ingress middleware tags route_id + tenant_id, approximate token_count using model config + input length, deterministic sampling via hash(tenant_id + request_id + day) < threshold, stream to Kafka -> redaction service -> short-term DB -> export job to S3. Need a small schema change and a new microservice for redaction/export. Pseudoconfig: 
```
audit_traces:
  sampling:
    mode: stable
    default_rate: 0.01
    tenant_overrides: true
  retention:
    hot_days: 14
    cold_days: 90
  redaction_patterns:
    - email
    - ssn
    - cc_number
```
Ethan (SRE): Pipeline must be async for not slowing requests. Backpressure policy: drop samples when stream lag > 30s and emit metric. SLO: sampling pipeline should not add >5ms p99 to the request path when async.
Nadia (Security): For exports, we should HMAC the file and store the key in KMS. Also rotate signing keys quarterly. Audit report should list patterns matched (counts) and redaction job version.
Priya (Compliance): Add checklist items: retention policy, redaction regex list, signed export, tenant opt-in consent, pilot customer sign-off. We'll review during pilot stage.
Ravi (Customer Success): I'll get FinReg's example fields and preferred schema (CSV/Parquet) and confirm acceptable sampling rates. Will push for parity with their internal audit format.
Sam (Solutions): I'll prototype the tile + modal and include a small help text about "estimated cost" vs "exact cost" for transparency.
Liam (Eng): Rough effort estimate: spike + POC = 2 sprints, pilot infra + console = 2 more sprints. If we scope to single-tenant pilot + aggregated export only, could compress to ~3 sprints. Known risks: redaction false negatives, storage blowout if sampling misconfigured, partial traces causing export confusion.
Maya (Product): Prioritization: where does this sit vs model-level cost allocation? FinReg is tied to a contract renewal, so this edges higher. We may shift some model-cost work later.
Ethan (SRE): Also call out cost-accounting caveat: quantized models and KV cache mean estimated token counts are best-effort. Document assumptions.
Nadia (Security): We should include automated redaction tests in CI and a weekly verification job that re-scans stored samples and emits a compliance report.
Priya (Compliance): Pilot acceptance criteria: 1) exportable traces for given date range, 2) redaction report generated, 3) signed export delivered, 4) product perf validated under load.
Maya (Product): Action items: 1) Ravi to get FinReg schema + acceptance (due Thu EOD), 2) Liam to write design doc + risk matrix (due next Tue), 3) Sam to share UI mock (due next Wed), 4) Nadia to outline security checklist + key rotation (due next Wed), 5) Ethan to propose retention/ops policy (due next Wed). I'll schedule a 30m sync after docs.
Ravi (Customer Success): On it. Will also ask if they need chain-of-custody logs for exports.
deploy-bot: Flag created: feature/audit-traces-export :white_check_mark:
Maya (Product): If design looks good we'll aim Q2 pilot. Success metrics: pilot customer can export traces (CSV/Parquet), redaction verification report available, console tile renders <200ms, and no >2% increase in request p99. Thanks all.
Liam (Eng): I'll call out mitigations for the risks in the doc and include a rollback plan for the pilot.
Ethan (SRE): Noted. Will also add a cost forecast for retention and exports to the infra checklist.
Maya (Product): Great. Sync invite sent for Mon. Closing thread for now.
